title: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari
hookLine: the Prophet's host in Medina, who, tradition says, was buried at the walls of Constantinople

cards: Middle of the night, in a two-story house in Medina. A man wakes and can't get back to sleep, because of where he's lying.
Right under his floor, his guest is sleeping, and the guest is the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him. Every step this man and his wife take up here, every shuffle, is over the Prophet's head.
So the two of them move into a corner and stay there till morning. Today: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and what it looks like to take a guest seriously.

teach.h: THE LOWER FLOOR IS EASIER FOR ME.
teach.b: Sahih Muslim tells it from Abu Ayyub himself. When the Prophet came to Medina, he stayed in Abu Ayyub's house. The Prophet chose the lower floor, and Abu Ayyub's family lived above.
After that sleepless night, Abu Ayyub went to him. The lower floor is easier for me, the Prophet explained.

teach.h: NOT ON A ROOF THAT YOU ARE UNDER.
teach.b: I will not go up onto a roof that you are under, Abu Ayyub answered. So the Prophet moved upstairs, and his host moved down. Then the food.
Abu Ayyub would send up meals, and when the dish came back, he would ask where the Prophet's fingers had been, and eat from that spot. One day the dish came back untouched. It had garlic in it.
Abu Ayyub went up, worried: is it forbidden? No, the Prophet said, but I don't like it.
Then, said Abu Ayyub, I dislike what you dislike. That's hosting with attention: noticing the floor, the plate, the smell of garlic. A good host keeps learning the guest.
Then the story jumps a long way forward.
The Sunan of Abu Dawud places Abu Ayyub with a Muslim army at Constantinople, explaining a verse of the Qur'an to the soldiers there.
Tradition says he died on that campaign and asked to be buried as close to the city's walls as they could reach.
The man who once wouldn't walk over the Prophet's head ended his life far from that house, still on the road.

how: Muslims tell Abu Ayyub's story from Sahih Muslim, where he hosts the Prophet in Medina, and remember him as a model of hospitality.

games.q: you are Abu Ayyub. your honored guest is sleeping downstairs, and you're walking over his head. what do you do?
o: keep quiet and tiptoe from now on.
ask him to move upstairs, and move down yourself.
move your family out of the house.
games.why: Muslim says the Prophet first preferred the lower floor, but Abu Ayyub said: I will not go up onto a roof you are under. so they swapped.

practice: Bring to mind someone who will be in your space soon: a visiting relative, a friend for coffee, a child coming home from school.
Picture them arriving, and ask what would make it easier for them: a free chair, a drink they like, your phone face down. If you pray, you can ask blessing on the people who come through your door.

wordCard.voice: Abu Ayyub. The man of Medina whose house sheltered the Prophet, and who, tradition says, was buried near the walls of Constantinople. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Abu Ayyub, the Ansari, one of the helpers of Medina.

carryVoice: Your line: the host. The floor, the plate, the garlic: he noticed it all. Until tomorrow.
